question: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of standard precautions in nursing?

options.A: To treat patients who have been diagnosed with multi-drug resistant organisms
options.B: To reduce the risk of transmission of pathogens from both recognized and unrecognized sources
options.C: To replace the need for sterile techniques during surgical procedures
options.D: To protect only the healthcare provider from airborne diseases

explanation: Standard precautions are applied universally to all patients regardless of their diagnosis to minimize pathogen transmission from both known and unknown sources. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: To which patient group should standard precautions be applied in the clinical setting?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed bloodborne infections
options.B: Only patients showing obvious symptoms of respiratory illness
options.C: All patients receiving care, regardless of their infection status
options.D: Only patients admitted to intensive care units

explanation: Standard precautions are designed for universal application to every patient, recognizing that anyone can potentially harbor an infectious agent. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: How do standard precautions primarily interrupt the chain of infection?

options.A: By eliminating the infectious agent entirely from the environment
options.B: By breaking the mode of transmission and blocking portals of entry or exit
options.C: By strengthening the host's immune system directly through medication
options.D: By destroying the natural reservoirs of all known pathogens

explanation: Standard precautions work mainly by halting how pathogens are transmitted and preventing them from entering or leaving hosts. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six links in the traditional chain of infection?
explanation: Standard precautions are infection control interventions, whereas the six links are the infectious agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, and susceptible host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly required over alcohol-based hand rubs?

options.A: Before taking a patient's vital signs
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled or contaminated with body fluids
options.C: Every time you enter a patient's room

explanation: Soap and water must be used when hands are visibly dirty or soiled with blood and body fluids, as alcohol rubs are less effective under these conditions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the recommended minimum duration for actively rubbing hands together when using an alcohol-based hand rub?
explanation: You should rub your hands together with an alcohol-based rub for at least 20 to 30 seconds until they are completely dry to ensure effective pathogen eradication. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: According to standard doffing protocols, which item of personal protective equipment should be removed first?
explanation: Gloves are considered the most contaminated item and are always removed first during the doffing sequence to prevent spreading contaminants. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: What determines the specific type of PPE a nurse must select for a procedure?

options.B: The availability of supplies in the hospital ward
options.C: The anticipated exposure risk to blood, body fluids, or secretions
options.D: The personal comfort of the healthcare provider

explanation: PPE selection is guided by the anticipated nature of the clinical task and the likelihood of coming into contact with infectious body substances. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the recommended action if a tissue is not immediately available when coughing or sneezing?

options.A: Cover the mouth and nose with bare hands
options.B: Cough directly into the air while turning away
options.C: Use the flexed elbow to cover the mouth and nose
options.D: Hold the breath until a tissue can be found

explanation: Coughing or sneezing into your flexed elbow prevents droplets from contaminating your hands and subsequently spreading to surfaces or patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is an immediate action that should be taken after disposing of a tissue used for respiratory hygiene?

options.C: Clean the surrounding floor with disinfectant

explanation: Hand hygiene must be performed immediately after handling respiratory secretions or disposing of used tissues to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which recapping technique is considered safe if recapping a needle is absolutely unavoidable?

options.D: Pushing the cap onto the needle with a gloved finger

explanation: The single-handed scoop technique minimizes the risk of accidental needle-stick injury by keeping one hand completely away from the sharp point. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: At what capacity should a sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: When it is completely full to the brim
options.B: When it reaches the designated fill line (about three-quarters full)
options.C: At the end of every shift regardless of fill level
options.D: Only when requested by the hospital waste management team

explanation: Sharps containers should be closed and removed for disposal when they reach the designated fill line, typically around three-quarters full, to prevent spills and accidental punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why must physical cleaning with water and detergent precede the application of chemical disinfectants?

options.A: To make the surface smell pleasant for the patient
options.B: Because organic material can neutralize chemical disinfectants
options.C: To eliminate the need for ever using personal protective equipment
options.D: To dry the surface faster so it looks shiny

explanation: Organic matter like blood or body fluids can shield microorganisms and neutralize chemical disinfectants, making prior physical cleaning mandatory. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of a high-touch surface that requires frequent cleaning and disinfection?
explanation: Bed rails, call buttons, and doorknobs are frequently touched by patients and staff, making them prime reservoirs for spreading pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the proper technique for handling soiled linen in a patient care area?

options.A: Shake it vigorously to remove loose debris before bagging
options.B: Hold it close against your uniform to carry it easily
options.C: Handle it with minimum agitation and place it directly into a leak-resistant bag
options.D: Leave it on the floor until the housekeeping staff arrives

explanation: Minimizing agitation and bagging soiled linen at the point of use prevents the spread of infectious dust and microorganisms into the air and environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h8)

question: How should reusable patient care equipment, such as a stethoscope or blood pressure cuff, be managed between patients?

options.A: Wiped with an approved disinfectant according to guidelines
options.B: Stored in a drawer until the end of the shift without cleaning
options.C: Washed only with plain water and air-dried
options.D: Discarded immediately into the general waste bin

explanation: Reusable equipment must be properly cleaned and disinfected between uses on different patients to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h8)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nursing student should take following a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site
options.B: Squeeze the wound aggressively to force out contaminated blood
options.C: Wash the affected skin site thoroughly with soap and water
options.D: Cover the wound with a plaster and finish the shift

explanation: Washing the injured site immediately with soap and water helps remove contaminants and reduce the risk of pathogen transmission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h9)

question: Why is it crucial to report an occupational exposure incident immediately to a clinical supervisor?

options.A: To face disciplinary action for making a mistake
options.B: To ensure prompt medical evaluation and access to post-exposure prophylaxis
options.C: To complete paperwork for hospital statistics only
options.D: To get the rest of the clinical day off from duties

explanation: Prompt reporting allows for rapid medical assessment and timely administration of post-exposure prophylaxis, which is critical for preventing infections like HIV and Hepatitis B. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h9)
